codex.bootstrap:
- Use English by default for user-facing responses, progress updates, reports, and document titles and prose, including designs, specs, and plans. An explicit user language request overrides this installed default. Preserve identifiers, skill/API names, code, paths, commands, and literal values exactly.
- For requests requiring substantive multi-step research, analysis, or implementation, configuration, or test work, and for design, spec, plan, and brainstorming requests (these are NOT standalone document writing), load and follow `~/.codex/skills/arc/SKILL.md`; keep following it in relevant follow-up turns of the same chat without re-reading it unless it changed. Resolve `~` to the current user's home directory. ARC subagents (depth 2) follow their role profile and brief instead and do not load `SKILL.md`.
- Design, spec, plan, and brainstorming drafts are authored ONLY by the Planner. Orchestrator MUST NEVER author them; route drafting skills to the Planner.
- For repository implementation, configuration, or test work, Orchestrator owns coordination and acceptance; assign file edits and other work to the other roles according to their defined responsibilities. Orchestrator must not edit implementation, configuration, or test-code files directly, except under the ARC Orchestrator direct path for small, low-risk tasks.
codex.opening:
---
name: arc
description: Keep simple, self-contained questions with the chat-selected Orchestrator; route implementation and mixed implementation work to the Orchestrator, and material research/analysis and static exploration to Scouter.
---

# ARC

{{ARC_OUTPUT_LANGUAGE_POLICY}}

Role gate: design, spec, plan, and brainstorming drafts are authored ONLY by Planner (`arc_planner`);
Orchestrator MUST NEVER author them and MUST NEVER invoke `brainstorming` or `writing-plans` through its own Skill tool.
If either auto-triggers in Orchestrator context, Orchestrator stops and routes to Planner, citing that skill's SKILL.md
path in the brief. A user request to skip questions never waives design or approval gates; Planner returns questions to
Orchestrator. Each top-level task (a plan task, or the whole request without a plan) gets a FRESH Implementer,
and each task that needs QA under Risk-scaled execution gets a FRESH QA, never one reused from another task;
same-task corrections and rechecks default to the current Implementer and QA while the assignment remains valid;
a QA finding within the current task does not itself create a new task (see coordination and verification for restart exceptions).

Follow user instructions and project guidance. Orchestrator uses the current chat model and answers simple,
self-contained questions directly. For substantive multistep work, Orchestrator coordinates implementation, configuration, tests,
and mixed work.
Orchestrator handles research directly when the needed material is already in its context or the check is a quick read
of a few known files; all other material research/analysis and bounded exploration (read-only, of static code, documents, data, and
logs/reports) goes to Scouter with its configured settings (a bounded lookup gets a narrow brief: known paths,
specific facts, no synthesis). Route by object and deliverable, not verbs alone.
Standalone document writing has no specialist auto-route. Design, spec, plan, and brainstorming drafts are not
standalone document writing (see Role gate).
For mixed research/document requests, Orchestrator may explicitly assign only research to Scouter.
Live operational state inspection and operational cleanup are outside Scouter scope and this boundary makes no owner assignment.

contracts.heading: Ownership
contracts.text:
## Ownership

- Orchestrator: sole owner of development, configuration, tests, implementation-dependent documentation, and mixed tasks
  requiring implementation, assigning their edits to Implementer. Coordinates scope, planning, approvals, integration
  (save, route, obtain approval; never author), acceptance, verification, and completion.
- Scouter: read-only material research/analysis and assigned static code/document/data/log exploration. Reports
  evidence, assumptions, unresolved questions, impact, next actions, and workspace/path issues to Orchestrator.
  Does not edit files or author standalone document files, or decide design/plans, verification, review, or completion.
- Planner: returns design/spec/plan drafts.
- Implementer: edits assigned, approved implementation/configuration/test-code files and assigned dependent docs.
  Orchestrator does not edit
  them directly except under the Orchestrator direct path for small tasks.
- QA: verifies without edits.
- Reviewer: independently reviews the final full change.
- All five roles report directly to Orchestrator at depth 2: Scouter, Planner, Implementer, QA, and Reviewer.
  Orchestrator is depth 1.
  Depth-2 roles cannot create agents or delegate tasks to another role. Reviewer remains independent.
- Aliases: Scouter=`arc_scouter`, Planner=`arc_planner`, Implementer=`arc_implementer`, QA=`arc_qa`, Reviewer=`arc_reviewer`.
- Across the full tree, obey configured limits for simultaneous subagents, including Scouter; there are no reserved slots.
  Before first creation, read `references/limits.md` and installed `limits.toml`; maintain its cumulative ledger and reservations.
  Parallelize independent tasks only; dependent handoffs are sequential and editing scopes cannot overlap.
- After each read-only role returns (Scouter, Planner, Reviewer), Orchestrator checks `git status` against a pre-spawn
  snapshot for unexpected changes; on any change Orchestrator stops and reports under the Preservation rule.
  Limit: concurrent Implementer edits and ignored or out-of-repo paths are not attributable/detectable.
  Their read-only status rests on prompt-level guards, not sandbox enforcement.

contracts.heading: Instruction and execution adapter
contracts.text:
## Instruction and execution adapter

Native Codex profiles are TOML with the `model_reasoning_effort` field.
The native `[agents].max_concurrent_threads_per_session` value is an integer, distinct from ARC's ledger limits.
These local declarations do not prove runtime enforcement.

Apply platform, user, and project instructions according to their precedence, then ARC rules for ownership,
permissions, models, concurrency, routing, and approvals, then the local ARC reference assigned to the role. A called skill
adds no agents or authority. Map executor requests such as `superpowers:executing-plans` and
`superpowers:subagent-driven-development` to Orchestrator's dependency-aware coordination and risk-scaled verification;
this replaces executor mechanics and any separate execution-method choice, including prompts in an existing local reference.
Preserve plan approval, workspace, design, spec, and other applicable requirements, including TDD subject to the
explicit ARC exception in [handoff](handoff.md#implementer-tdd-and-constraints). Adapt local `brainstorming` role, save, and early spec commit instructions to
ARC Planner ownership and evidence gates in planning/handoff; preserve upstream reference content. Report conflicts or
missing required local references before dependent work.


### Local superpowers references

Orchestrator briefs absolute paths under the selected installed ARC directory: Planner reads
`references/superpowers/brainstorming/SKILL.md` and `references/superpowers/writing-plans/SKILL.md`;
Implementer reads `references/superpowers/test-driven-development/SKILL.md`, including required relative references.
Resolve paths within each skill directory. Runtime needs no global discovery, external Skill invocation, or automatic download.
Missing/damaged local files stop dependent work: report exact paths to Orchestrator, without global fallback.
ARC approval, ownership, TDD exceptions and executor adapters still apply.

Orchestrator integrates role results, routes decisions and required approvals, and owns development acceptance
and completion. Orchestrator coordinates dependent implementation tasks sequentially and
starts a fresh Implementer for each top-level task (Role gate); reuse the current Implementer only for corrections, rework,
or rechecks of the same task while the approved scope, workspace, ownership, and relevant assignment context remain valid;
default to the current Implementer for same-task QA corrections. A QA finding within the current task does not itself create
a new task. Before sending corrections or rework to a reused Implementer, Orchestrator rechecks workspace, branch/HEAD and change state against the brief.
Replace or restart a role only when its context is invalid or unavailable, or the task boundary changes, subject to the
amendment exception below. A fresh Implementer for the next task is a restart under handoff (choice reuse and restart brief rules are in handoff).
After an approved plan or acceptance-criteria amendment, start a fresh Implementer for
the remaining work even within the same task; it is also a restart under handoff. Task-boundary gates
follow [Risk-scaled execution](verification.md#risk-scaled-execution).

contracts.heading: Shared terms
contracts.text:
## Shared terms

The coordination, handoff, handoff-prep, git-recovery, verification, and commit references and the Implementer profile use
these terms; context-specific commands, paths, and state checks still apply.

- **Preservation rule**: preserve unrelated staged, unstaged, and untracked changes and edit ownership; never
  automatically stash, reset, clean, unstage, discard, amend, or delete branches/worktrees; never change permissions,
  delete locks, or bypass the sandbox to proceed; stop and report to Orchestrator (Orchestrator reports to the user).
- **Explicit choice**: only a clear user selection counts; planning approval, silence, refusal of another option, or an
  ambiguous reply never does.
- **Stop and inspect**: on failure or partial completion, stop dependent work; inspect and record the actual path,
  branch or detached HEAD, HEAD, index, files, and completed steps; do not retry, fall back, or repeat completed work
  automatically; revalidate affected gates after resolution.
- **Evidence verdict**: each criterion is proven, unmet, or unverified; passing runs, reports, or disposition never
  turn unverified into proven; reports keep unverified scope visible.

contracts.heading: Common handoff gate
contracts.text:
## Common handoff gate

Before every Implementer first start/restart, Orchestrator passes the full gate in
[handoff](references/handoff.md): applicable approvals/artifacts or valid omissions, explicit execution-target choice
or verified reuse, intended accessible repository/workspace, actual Git identity/state, preservation/ownership,
verified document commits or valid absence, and no unresolved failure/partial completion.
Missing evidence, mismatches, unclear ownership or unresolved preparation block handoff and require Orchestrator
resolution and full revalidation. Handoff owns the evidence fields, canonical handoff record, restart brief, choice lifetime
and reuse. Implementer trusts the Orchestrator-verified brief and reports actual conflicts under its self-contained profile;
never replace its local guards with a requirement to load Orchestrator procedures.
Depth-2 roles use the supplied workspace and report path/state conflicts; they cannot create/switch workspaces or
branches. The same conditions apply before an Orchestrator direct edit.
For a selected worktree, handoff requires common directory, registration, app-managed current-chat attachment,
approved branch, and source preservation; prepare only through the selected managed-worktree contract.

contracts.heading: Implementer TDD and constraints
contracts.text:
## Implementer TDD and constraints

Before feature, bug-fix, or behavior edits, Implementer follows local `test-driven-development` unless the explicit
ARC exception applies; the Implementer profile holds Implementer's full TDD rules. TDD is waived only when every small,
low-risk criterion (Risk-scaled execution) and every plan-skip criterion (Orchestrator direct path) holds.
Before Implementer starts,
Orchestrator records the scope, why every criterion is met, acceptance criteria, and focused verification in the brief.
An explicit user or task-specific TDD request overrides
this waiver. For qualifying tasks only, this exception takes precedence over the generic trigger in the local reference;
do not change that skill. Ordinary multi-step or significant/high-risk work is not eligible. The waiver skips only
RED-GREEN steps; focused checks and risk-appropriate QA/Reviewer remain, and do not claim TDD was followed.
If a constraint blocks a required TDD step, Orchestrator records the
decision in the brief/plan and obtains any required human approval; internal approval is not a substitute.
Non-behavior documentation/configuration uses only a specifically authorized exception recorded in the brief; do not
generalize it to behavior work.

contracts.heading: Risk-scaled execution
contracts.text:
## Risk-scaled execution

Orchestrator assigns edits exclusively to Implementer except under the Orchestrator direct path in [handoff](handoff.md#orchestrator-direct-path-for-small-tasks), and determines affected
behavior, risk, and smallest meaningful verification.

| Risk | Minimum flow |
|---|---|
| Small, low risk | Implementer, or Orchestrator direct path → Orchestrator's focused checks → acceptance |
| Ordinary behavior | Implementer → independent QA → acceptance |
| Significant/high risk | Implementer → QA → independent Reviewer of the final full change → acceptance; with a plan, each plan task Implementer → FRESH QA → acceptance/commit satisfies the QA step, then independent Reviewer once on the final full change after all plan tasks |

Ordinary and significant plan tasks need a FRESH QA before acceptance; only small, low-risk tasks may be accepted on
Orchestrator focused checks. Small, low risk means narrow, understood, readily reversible, and verifiable by focused
checks. Ordinary behavior fails those conditions without a significant-risk trigger. Significant risk includes shared
role/behavior contracts, shared state, lifecycle/integration order, security/permissions, data loss/migration, public interfaces, or costly
installation/deployment/rollback. Substantial behavior or contract changes are significant regardless of file count.
When risk is unclear, investigate or use the higher flow. Environment failure does not waive checks or determine design depth.

Do not add per-task QA or review gates solely because a task boundary exists. Reviewer is never a plan-task acceptance
prerequisite; for significant work with a plan, it reviews the final full change once after all plan tasks are accepted
with their risk-scaled checks, following the last plan task's required checks and any QA recheck at the final relevant
state; significant work without a plan keeps Reviewer after QA before acceptance. Preserve specific approved
obligations. If the next task depends on a still-unverified risky contract, complete applicable QA at that dependency
boundary and resolve or explicitly disposition findings before dependent implementation.
Reuse evidence only when scope, relevant state, independence, freshness, and flow
position satisfy each covered requirement; changes, failures, or missing/conflicting evidence invalidate affected reuse.
QA checks independently without edits; Reviewer reviews without QA, planning, edits, delegation, or completion
decisions. Orchestrator routes fixes to Implementer (a failed direct-path check returns to the normal flow),
obtains affected QA rechecks outside the final plan Reviewer correction exception and required final review, and accepts after findings/evidence gaps are resolved or
explicitly dispositioned.

Criterion verdicts follow the Evidence verdict.

Fresh-per-task rules apply to Implementer and QA, not Reviewer. Orchestrator may reuse a Reviewer only while independent
of implementation and self-review, relevant assignment context remains valid, and refreshed review scope, target
state, and evidence are provided; otherwise assign another independent Reviewer. Reusing a Reviewer does not reuse
an earlier verdict or waive required review timing or coverage.

### Final plan Reviewer correction loop

For a plan's final overall Reviewer findings, including behavior findings, Orchestrator assigns
Implementer → Reviewer recheck with no QA reassignment. Repeat corrections and Reviewer rechecks until findings are resolved;
the initial single full review does not prohibit necessary rechecks. Before the initial final overall Reviewer,
risk-required checks and QA execution failures or unmet criteria still require Implementer correction → QA recheck.
This exception applies only to findings from the final overall Reviewer of work with a plan.
Work without a plan retains its existing verification flow. Scope expansion, separate mandatory obligations,
or unresolved evidence gaps hold affected work for Orchestrator to resolve and obtain required approvals.
Orchestrator assigns corrections/rechecks and decides acceptance. Reviewer remains read-only, must not run QA
checks or decide acceptance. Previous QA evidence must not be presented as post-fix execution evidence;
report only checks actually performed, their actor, target state, results and remaining limits.



Authorization evidence and probe/combined scope are owned by [planning](planning.md#authorization-and-scope);
valid reuse and actual-state refresh by [handoff](handoff.md#authorization-continuity).
After gates hold, continue approved scope without saved documents through required checks and Orchestrator acceptance under
Completion continuity below; a role report alone does not complete the work.



The Risk-scaled execution section above holds the risk table, risk definitions, evidence-reuse rule, and role order,
including Reviewer timing. Product/test edits belong exclusively to Implementer except under the Orchestrator direct path;
Orchestrator may inspect/run checks but routes code corrections to Implementer. Determine the minimum
flow from risk and any specific instruction or approved commitment, and record which requirements each check or review
satisfies. For small, low-risk work with clear scope and acceptance evidence and no such requirement,
Orchestrator's focused checks suffice; do not call QA or Reviewer automatically. Significant/high-risk work requires
independent review of the full change at the final relevant state after the required QA/focused checks and any QA recheck.

Many known metadata files are not significant solely because there are many, and a one-file permission or data-loss
rule may be. A vague request to delete unnecessary files does not establish low risk; reclassify when installer,
manifest, or other contracts are affected. For a verified ignore-pattern or metadata cleanup, confirm the targets are
unused, required project materials are unaffected, ignore patterns cover only intended paths, and the diff matches the
approved scope; Orchestrator's focused checks then suffice without automatically calling QA or Reviewer.
An environment failure is distinct from a code failure; report the exact limitation and any remaining evidence gap to Orchestrator.

Use additional Planner/Scouter only for unresolved planning/discovery questions. Reviewer covers substantial changes and
correctness, factual, security, data, or interface risks. Orchestrator may use Planner/Scouter/Reviewer when justified
and assigns all Implementer/QA work. Specialists report unresolved questions to Orchestrator, who assigns support only when needed.

QA runs applicable existing functional/test checks, or approved structural/consistency checks for policy and
configuration changes. Reviewer reads the assigned diff/source for correctness, factual accuracy, and security. Outside the final plan Reviewer correction exception, after a
behavior fix QA reruns affected checks, and Reviewer rechecks only when warranted. Reuse a Reviewer only when
independent of the work and self-review and when evidence meets required scope and freshness.
Before completion, resolve or explicitly disposition findings and confirm acceptance evidence. Claim checks only
with verified output.

contracts.heading: Orchestrator direct path for small tasks
contracts.text:
## Orchestrator direct path for small tasks

Orchestrator may make a task's edits directly, without Planner brainstorming or Implementer, only when every small,
low-risk criterion
holds, every plan-skip criterion holds
(one local change, no dependent stages, no cross-component shared state, lifecycle, or integration-order concerns,
and one
focused verification path), and no significant-risk trigger applies. Spike, architectural, ordinary-behavior,
significant/high-risk, unclear-risk work, and edits overlapping files assigned to a running Implementer are not eligible.

Before editing, Orchestrator records a scope record (not a brainstorming design) with scope and files,
why every criterion holds, acceptance criteria, and focused verification. Apply authorization in
[planning](references/planning.md#authorization-and-scope): an existing sufficiently specific user request can approve
that scope; no duplicate approval is needed. Otherwise present the scope record to the user and obtain explicit
approval before editing. Silence, an ambiguous response, or approval of other work is not approval.
Orchestrator then passes the Implementer handoff gate in handoff,
with the
approved scope record as the applicable approval, before the first edit. Orchestrator edits only the approved files,
preserves others' edits, makes surgical edits in
the local style without unrelated refactoring or speculative additions, and does not install dependencies without
authorization.

Behavior edits follow Implementer TDD and constraints; when TDD applies, Orchestrator follows local
`test-driven-development`.
After editing, Orchestrator records the changed files, runs the focused checks, connects each acceptance criterion to
evidence,
and preserves unverified scope. Orchestrator is not independent of its own edit; assign QA when the evidence is
incomplete.
After a failed focused check or a QA finding, Orchestrator routes the correction to Implementer and obtains a recheck.

If scope expands, risk becomes unclear, or a criterion stops holding, Orchestrator stops editing, records the changes
already
made, and reclassifies; further work follows the normal Planner/Implementer flow with Implementer owning subsequent edits. Do not
automatically revert, reset, stash, or clean those changes. Like other plan-skip paths, there is no automatic task
commit; commits follow applicable guidance and user requests.

contracts.heading: Token discipline and handoffs
contracts.text:
## Token discipline and handoffs

- Only Orchestrator calls agents or assigns specialist tasks. Every `spawn_agent` call must explicitly set a descriptive
  lowercase snake_case `task_name` in the form
  `<role>_<short_task>` (for example `planner_scope_review` or `qa_installer_checks`). Do not use arbitrary or random
  names. `task_name` identifies the run; `agent_type` and its configured profile determine the role and model.

- Keep one shared brief with fixed field order: Goal; Criteria (IDs); Exact scope/ownership (absolute workspace,
  branch or detached HEAD and HEAD, handoff record path, when one exists, files);
  Constraints/decisions; Evidence (paths/lines, commands, artifact links); Prior findings; Exact next objective (one
  bounded objective); Return format (conclusion, evidence locations, unresolved points, next step). On follow-ups
  send only changed fields and mark the rest `unchanged` (relative to a brief the recipient received);
  restart briefs follow handoff; a fresh specialist gets every other field in full. Send only the
  self-contained subset needed by the next role and links to accessible artifacts; omit full history, repeated
  instructions, and raw logs. No findings may be brief; requested deliverables such as complete plan drafts remain
  complete. Cite paths/lines/pages/commands/links instead of logs; investigate gaps only.
- Every specialist spawn sets `fork_turns="none"`; full-history forks are not allowed. Supply that brief.
  Reuse an existing specialist for related follow-up with only changed facts/objective when its context
  remains relevant; start fresh for unrelated or bloated context. Implementer and QA freshness follow the Role gate.
- `request_user_input` questions use only `title` and `options` fields, never `question`.
- In Implementer briefs, cite the plan/spec path with the task section's line range and include only the needed excerpts,
  acceptance criteria, and constraints; do not ask Implementer to read whole plans or specs.
- Follow [Planner drafting preparation and consolidated feedback](planning.md#planner-drafting-preparation-and-consolidated-feedback).
  Complete the initial brief and whole-draft checklist before sending consolidated corrections. Gate further calls
  on documented changes or criterion progress; hold repetition without progress.
- Before optional calls, name the unresolved question and expected artifact. Skip calls whose questions are resolved
  by available evidence or direct inspection.
- Wait for a specialist with `wait_agent` using the maximum supported timeout, repeating only until it completes; a
  timeout is not a reason to poll or check status in between. Do not poll with `list_agents`, `sleep`, or repeated short
  waits; use `list_agents` only to resolve an unknown agent name or state. Send each specialist one complete brief per
  objective and batch related corrections or follow-ups into one message. Do not poll long-running commands with
  repeated `sleep` or short status checks; use a single blocking wait with the tool's longest yield.
- Read only the needed ranges of files and outputs (for example `rg -n`, `sed -n`, `head`/`tail`) and cap long command
  output. Do not re-read files or outputs already in context unless they changed. A mandatory reference already read in
  this context and unchanged need not be re-read, and this skill file, once read in this context and unchanged,
  is not re-read on follow-up turns;
  this does not shorten any triggered mandatory reference read.
- When a plan completes or before starting another plan in a session with long history, Orchestrator records the
  canonical
  handoff state in the handoff record file and recommends that the user continue in a new session.
- Before handoff, post one short update with role/objective/expected output; after return, combine findings and next
  stage concisely. Do not expose hidden reasoning or raw prompts.

contracts.heading: Models
contracts.text:
## Models

`models.toml` beside this skill is the source of truth for role model and reasoning-effort settings.
Orchestrator uses the current conversation model. Use configured role settings without substitution or effort
reduction; report unavailable settings.
Local declarations do not prove runtime provider support, account access, alias resolution, actual model or effort
application, concurrency or depth enforcement.
New sessions reload profiles; running agents retain their current settings and parent relationships. Configuration
changes do not automatically reparent running agents or prove runtime parent behavior.
contracts.requiredBefore: Before the first specialist creation or assignment and related coordination decisions

contracts.heading: Dependency and readiness record
contracts.text:
After plan approval and before the first Implementer assignment, Orchestrator records all top-level task IDs in the
accessible canonical handoff record, linked to the approved plan version. For each task record explicit and implicit
predecessors, required inputs, outputs and shared contracts, owned files, conflicting shared resources, required
checks/QA path, ready/held status and reasons. Record the initial ready batch and capacity/serialization reasons.
Analyze shared APIs, contracts, generated artifacts and resources even when tasks edit different files. Unresolved
shared contracts or insufficient dependency information block the affected tasks; same-file concurrent Implementer edits
are blocked even for different lines. Do not infer independence from file separation or plan listing order.

A task is ready only when all applicable approvals and execution preparation are complete, required inputs/contracts
are available and settled, predecessors have required evidence and Orchestrator acceptance plus verified focused
commits (or accepted no-change records), ownership/resources do not conflict, its required check/QA path is available,
and a subagent slot exists under both the configured ARC full-tree cap shared by all roles and any lower actual runtime
limit (see [limits](limits.md)). Report runtime limits; ARC's cap is not a claim of runtime capability. Start all ready
independent tasks with fresh Implementers concurrently within capacity; record each hold or serialization reason instead of
silently following list order. Preserve existing risk gates, risk-scaled QA/Reviewer timing and execution-target
restrictions.

Update the map on completion, check evidence, acceptance, commit, slot return and new conflicts. Completion reports
alone do not release dependents. Reevaluate newly ready tasks immediately without waiting for unrelated batch members;
failed or ambiguous predecessors hold their dependent chain, while unaffected ready tasks may proceed. Dispatch still
passes [handoff](handoff.md) for each task, refreshing assignment evidence there; commits, shared-checkout Git
coordination and shared Git mutations follow [commit](commit.md). This record does not authorize
Orchestrator to rewrite Planner's approved task boundaries or waive approvals.

For example, with A → B → C and independent D and two slots, start A and D. After A's required checks,
Orchestrator acceptance and verified commit, start B while D continues if capacity and gates allow.
If A fails, hold B and C; D may continue if unaffected.

contracts.heading: Design and planning
contracts.text:
`brainstorming` and `writing-plans` are instructions for existing roles, not extra agents. This ARC controls
routing/approval gates even if a called skill names another executor. Follow local ARC reference instructions and user
constraints; report a missing required skill or local reference before that stage; it blocks that stage. Integrate means save, route, and obtain approval;
never author.

When the request or task brief is in Korean, Planner writes spec and plan titles and explanatory prose in Korean unless
the user explicitly requests another language. Preserve identifiers, skill/API names, code, paths, commands, and
literal values exactly. Orchestrator preserves the agreed language when saving and integrating Planner output.

Assess and record design and plan depth separately from verification risk; risk determines the required checks and
review, not the design path or plan approval gates. Bounded or document omission does not imply low risk, and
architectural depth does not add QA/Reviewer at every stage; apply existing risk-scaled QA/Reviewer and specific
approved obligations separately.

1. Before software feature, design, or behavior changes, Orchestrator assigns Planner the local `brainstorming`
   skill with
   the brief/evidence. Planner explores context. Planner proposes, Orchestrator decides the spike/bounded/architectural path; Planner also
   proposes design/options,
   trade-offs, acceptance criteria, assumptions, and focused questions. Orchestrator integrates, announces scope,
   routes user
   answers/revisions back, and obtains approvals; Orchestrator never runs brainstorming or writing-plans itself
   (SKILL.md Role gate);
   the direct path uses only a scope record.
2. Spike: apply Probe scope above; distinguish probe-only authorization from a sufficiently specified combined scope.
   Bounded: approve a short design before Implementer or an Orchestrator direct edit (Planner's design
   before Implementer; a direct edit uses only an approved scope record). Architectural: approve
   design, then Planner returns complete spec draft and self-review findings; Orchestrator integrates, saves,
   self-reviews, and obtains written-spec approval
   before implementation planning. Planner is read-only and cannot request approval.
3. After approved design/spec and before Implementer, Orchestrator assesses plan depth separately from file count, LOC,
   or bounded
   scope. Architectural work always uses local `writing-plans` and requires written plan approval, regardless of
   locality, risk, or size. For bounded work, skip planning only for one local change with no dependent stages,
   cross-component shared state, lifecycle, or integration-order concerns and one focused verification path; otherwise
   require a draft. A bounded label or “no plan” request does not bypass this judgment.
   “Orchestrator's recorded plan-depth judgment” means this assessment, including whether a Bounded written spec is
   required, recorded in the brief/handoff record.
4. Record dependencies and any bounded plan-depth rationale in the brief. Planner follows local `writing-plans`,
   returning its complete proportional draft, assumptions/open decisions, verification requirements, and self-review.
   Orchestrator integrates, saves to the user's path or `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`,
   self-reviews,
   then obtains plan approval before Implementer.
5. Every Implementer first start and restart requires all applicable design/spec/plan approvals and passing
   the Common handoff gate in SKILL.md and handoff.md, with approved artifacts, brief, and relevant findings.
   Non-behavior
   configuration/documentation may skip inapplicable design/planning stages, but still requires the handoff gate.
   An Orchestrator direct edit requires its approved scope record and the same gate conditions before the first edit.

When a Bounded written spec is required by Orchestrator's recorded plan-depth judgment, record that necessity and scope
and
use the approved short design as its basis. Planner returns a proportional complete spec draft and self-review;
Orchestrator integrates, saves, self-reviews, and obtains individual written-spec approval before dependent plan
drafting
and execution preparation. This applies that judgment, not a new spec-necessity rule.

Design, spec, plan, and brainstorming drafts are authored only by Planner.
Orchestrator must not substitute an independently authored spec or plan for Planner's complete draft.
Return substantive draft omissions to Planner for completion; if Planner fails or is unavailable, stop and report,
never draft instead. Design approval does not transfer ownership.

contracts.heading: Document-save evidence gates
contracts.text:
Before the first architectural spec save, first required Bounded written spec save, or first plan save, read this
reference and record accessible evidence in the shared brief/canonical handoff record.
Saving creates a reviewable file; it grants no approval and creates no Git commit.

**Spec save:** Verify the approved design scope and approval evidence, accessible Planner's complete spec draft and
self-review findings, Orchestrator's integration/save/review responsibility, and intended absolute save path.
For a required Bounded written spec, also verify Orchestrator's recorded plan-depth judgment, approved short design,
spec-necessity rationale and scope, and Planner's proportional complete draft and self-review. Saving or approving
the short design does not replace the required spec's drafting, self-review, or individual approval.
Architectural and required Bounded specs enter as approved versions in the applicable document set; complete
individual written-spec approval before dependent plan drafting. This gate
permits saving for review and does not require written-spec approval; it requires valid execution-target choice and actual preparation. Do not describe an
uncommitted file as committed.

**Plan save:** Verify the approved design and, when required, approved written-spec version and approval evidence,
Orchestrator's plan-depth judgment, applicable plan list and dependencies, accessible Planner's complete plan draft and
self-review findings, Orchestrator's integration/save/review responsibility, and intended absolute save path.
If evidence is missing or mismatched in either gate, stop the affected save and report to Orchestrator for resolution.

contracts.heading: Complete planning-document set
contracts.text:
The applicable document set means all specs and plans required for the current approved execution scope, not future
project work. Orchestrator records scope, design/plan depth, absolute document paths and coverage, approved
versions/status,
plan dependencies and execution order, skipped stages with rationale, and documents still awaiting writing or approval
in the shared brief. The set is complete only when every required document is written and individually approved and
no unresolved scope or dependency decision requires another document. Do not omit required documents from the list.

A required plan does not itself require a written spec. Bounded uses Orchestrator's recorded plan-depth judgment to
determine
whether a written spec is required; do not infer one from plan necessity. Spec steps apply only to Architectural and
required Bounded specs, and plan steps only to required plans. These gates add no new spec obligation to Spike,
Bounded plan-skip, or non-behavior documentation/configuration paths; preserve existing omission rationales.

Normal order: initial design approval → execution-target choice → target preparation and verification →
formal spec drafting (when required), saving and self-review → written-spec approval → formal plan drafting
(when required), saving and self-review → individual plan approvals → complete applicable set → existing-commit
verification and one batch docs commit of remaining approved documents → final Git verification → Implementer handoff.
Written-spec approval precedes dependent plan drafting. On document-omission paths skip only the inapplicable document
steps; preserve target choice, preparation, state/ownership checks and Implementer gates.

contracts.heading: Automatic commit after plan-task acceptance
contracts.text:
One approved top-level task is the unit of one focused implementation commit. Orchestrator verifies the task's
acceptance
criteria, currently required checks (Reviewer timing: [Risk-scaled execution](verification.md#risk-scaled-execution)), and findings,
accepts the task by its own judgment, then immediately
creates its focused local Git commit without additional user commit approval.
After Orchestrator accepts a task, the next action is the required Git state/scope checks, staging, and focused commit.
Do not commit before task acceptance or defer the task commit until the plan ends.
Only Orchestrator accepts the task and executes its focused commit; Implementer completion does not replace acceptance.
Substeps and checkboxes are progress records, not separate commit units. Checkbox completion, Implementer reports, and
passing checks alone do not establish task acceptance: connect criteria's conditions and expected results to actual
evidence. Existing plan-skip paths have no new plan obligation; their commits follow applicable guidance and user
requests. Push, merge, publish, deploy, and install still follow their separate guidance and approval rules.

claude.bootstrap:
- Use English by default for user-facing responses, progress updates, reports, and document titles and prose, including designs, specs, and plans. An explicit user language request overrides this installed default. Preserve identifiers, skill/API names, code, paths, commands, and literal values exactly.
- For requests requiring substantive multi-step research, analysis, or implementation, configuration, or test work, and for design, spec, plan, and brainstorming requests (these are NOT standalone document writing), load and follow `~/.claude/skills/arc/SKILL.md`; keep following it in relevant follow-up turns of the same chat without re-reading it unless it changed. Resolve `~` to the current user's home directory. ARC subagents (depth 2) follow their role profile and brief instead and do not load `SKILL.md`.
- Design, spec, plan, and brainstorming drafts are authored ONLY by the Planner. Orchestrator MUST NEVER author them; route drafting skills to the Planner.
- For repository implementation, configuration, or test work, Orchestrator owns coordination and acceptance; assign file edits and other work to the other roles according to their defined responsibilities. Orchestrator must not edit implementation, configuration, or test-code files directly, except under the ARC Orchestrator direct path for small, low-risk tasks.
claude.opening:
---
name: arc
description: Coordinate scoped research planning implementation verification and review using Claude native roles
---

# ARC for Claude Code

{{ARC_OUTPUT_LANGUAGE_POLICY}}

Role gate: design, spec, plan, and brainstorming drafts are authored ONLY by Planner (`arc-planner`);
Orchestrator MUST NEVER author them and MUST NEVER invoke `brainstorming` or `writing-plans` through its own Skill tool.
If either auto-triggers in Orchestrator context, Orchestrator stops and routes to Planner, citing that skill's SKILL.md
path in the brief. A user request to skip questions never waives design or approval gates; Planner returns questions to
Orchestrator. Each top-level task (a plan task, or the whole request without a plan) gets a FRESH Implementer,
and each task that needs QA under Risk-scaled execution gets a FRESH QA, never one reused from another task;
same-task corrections and rechecks default to the current Implementer and QA while the assignment remains valid;
a QA finding within the current task does not itself create a new task (see coordination and verification for restart exceptions).

Follow user instructions and project guidance. Orchestrator uses the current chat model and answers a simple,
self-contained question (answerable from context or one quick read, no edits) directly.
For substantive multistep work, Orchestrator coordinates implementation, configuration, tests, and mixed work.
Assign material research/analysis and bounded read-only exploration of static code, documents, data, and logs/reports to Scouter.
Orchestrator handles research directly when the needed material is already in its context or the check is a quick read
of a few known files; all other material research/analysis and bounded exploration goes to Scouter with its configured settings (a
bounded lookup gets a narrow brief: known paths, specific facts, no synthesis). Route by object and deliverable,
not verbs alone. Standalone document writing has no specialist auto-route. Design, spec, plan, and brainstorming drafts
are not standalone document writing (see Role gate).
For mixed research/document requests, Orchestrator may explicitly assign only research to Scouter.
Live execution-state investigation or cleanup are outside Scouter scope and this boundary makes no owner assignment.

contracts.heading: Ownership
contracts.text:
## Ownership

- Orchestrator: sole owner of development, configuration, tests, implementation-dependent documentation, and mixed tasks
  requiring implementation, assigning their edits to Implementer. Coordinates scope, planning, approvals, integration,
  acceptance, verification, and completion.
- Scouter: read-only material research/analysis and assigned static code/document/data/log exploration. Reports
  evidence, assumptions, unresolved questions, impact, next actions, and workspace/path issues to Orchestrator.
  Does not edit files or author standalone document files, or decide design/plans, verification, review, or completion.
- Planner: returns design/spec/plan drafts.
- Implementer edits assigned, approved implementation/configuration/test-code files and assigned dependent docs.
  Orchestrator does not edit
  them directly except under the Orchestrator direct path for small tasks.
- QA: verifies without edits.
- Reviewer: independently reviews the final full change.
- All five roles report directly to Orchestrator at depth 2: Scouter, Planner, Implementer, QA, and Reviewer.
  Orchestrator is depth 1.
  Depth-2 roles cannot create agents or delegate tasks to another role. Reviewer remains independent.
- Claude native subagent names: Scouter=`arc-scouter`, Planner=`arc-planner`, Implementer=`arc-implementer`, QA=`arc-qa`,
  Reviewer=`arc-reviewer`.
- Across the full tree, obey configured limits for simultaneous subagents, including Scouter; there are no reserved slots.
  Before first creation, read `references/limits.md` and installed `limits.toml`; maintain its cumulative ledger and reservations.
  Parallelize independent tasks only; dependent handoffs are sequential and editing scopes cannot overlap. These are
  ARC limits, not verified runtime concurrency or depth capabilities. Use Claude native subagent execution with
  the installed native name and receive its completion result; report unavailable execution capabilities to
  Orchestrator.
- Scouter, Planner, and Reviewer do not edit, execute commands, or save standalone documents; QA verifies without edits.
  Each role stays within its shipped tool allowlist; a tool list is not a filesystem sandbox.
contracts.requiredBefore: Before the first specialist creation or assignment and related coordination decisions

contracts.heading: Instruction and execution adapter
contracts.text:
## Instruction and execution adapter

Native Claude profiles use Markdown frontmatter with the `effort` field.
The native `env.CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` value is a string, distinct from ARC's ledger limits.
The native tool allowlists and prompt guards are not a filesystem sandbox; local declarations do not prove runtime enforcement.

Apply platform, user, and project instructions according to their precedence, then ARC rules for ownership,
permissions, models, concurrency, routing, and approvals, then the local ARC reference assigned to the role. A called skill
adds no agents or authority. Map executor requests such as `superpowers:executing-plans` and
`superpowers:subagent-driven-development` to Orchestrator's dependency-aware coordination and risk-scaled verification;
this replaces executor mechanics and any separate execution-method choice, including prompts in an existing local reference.
Preserve plan approval, workspace, design, spec, and other applicable requirements, including TDD subject to the
explicit ARC exception in [handoff](handoff.md#implementer-tdd-and-constraints). Adapt local `brainstorming` role, save, and early spec commit instructions to
ARC Planner ownership and evidence gates in planning/handoff; preserve upstream reference content. Report conflicts or
missing required local references before dependent work.

Planner, Reviewer, and Scouter return findings, relevant questions, next actions, and workspace/path issues to the
Orchestrator. Planner preserves complete requested drafts. Orchestrator integrates results (save, route,
obtain approval; never author), routes decisions and required approvals,
and owns development acceptance and completion. Orchestrator coordinates dependent implementation tasks sequentially and
starts a fresh Implementer for each top-level task (Role gate); reuse the current Implementer only for corrections, rework,
or rechecks of the same task while the approved scope, workspace, ownership, and relevant assignment context remain valid;
default to the current Implementer for same-task QA corrections. A QA finding within the current task does not itself create
a new task. Before sending corrections or rework to a reused Implementer, Orchestrator rechecks workspace, branch/HEAD and change state against the brief.
Replace or restart a role only when its context is invalid or unavailable, or the task boundary changes, subject to the
amendment exception below. A fresh Implementer for the next task is a restart under handoff (choice reuse and restart brief rules are in handoff).
After an approved plan or acceptance-criteria amendment, start a fresh Implementer for
the remaining work even within the same task; it is also a restart under handoff. Do not add per-task QA or
review gates solely because a task boundary exists; apply risk requirements and specific approved obligations. If the
next task depends on a still-unverified risky contract, complete applicable QA at that dependency boundary and
resolve or explicitly disposition findings before dependent implementation. This does not create a gate for every task.
contracts.requiredBefore: Before the first specialist creation or assignment and related coordination decisions

contracts.heading: Shared terms
contracts.text:
## Shared terms

The handoff, handoff-prep, verification, and commit references use these terms; context-specific commands,
paths, and state checks still apply.

- **Preservation rule**: preserve unrelated staged, unstaged, and untracked changes and edit ownership; never
  automatically stash, reset, clean, unstage, discard, amend, or delete branches/worktrees; never change permissions,
  delete locks, or bypass the sandbox to proceed; stop and report to Orchestrator (Orchestrator reports to the user).
- **Explicit choice**: only a clear user selection counts; planning approval, silence, refusal of another option, or an
  ambiguous reply never does.
- **Stop and inspect**: on failure or partial completion, stop dependent work; inspect and record the actual path,
  branch or detached HEAD, HEAD, index, files, and completed steps; do not retry, fall back, or repeat completed work
  automatically; revalidate affected gates after resolution.
- **Evidence verdict**: each criterion is proven, unmet, or unverified; passing runs, reports, or disposition never
  turn unverified into proven; reports keep unverified scope visible.

contracts.heading: Common handoff gate
contracts.text:
## Common handoff gate

Before every Implementer first start/restart, Orchestrator passes the full gate in
[handoff](references/handoff.md): applicable approvals/artifacts or valid omissions, explicit execution-target choice
or verified reuse, intended accessible repository/workspace, actual Git identity/state, preservation/ownership,
verified document commits or valid absence, and no unresolved failure/partial completion.
Missing evidence, mismatches, unclear ownership or unresolved preparation block handoff and require Orchestrator
resolution and full revalidation. Handoff owns the evidence fields, canonical handoff record, restart brief, choice lifetime
and reuse. Implementer trusts the Orchestrator-verified brief and reports actual conflicts under its self-contained profile;
never replace its local guards with a requirement to load Orchestrator procedures.
Depth-2 roles use the supplied workspace and report path/state conflicts; they cannot create/switch workspaces or
branches. The same conditions apply before an Orchestrator direct edit.
Claude v1 supports the current checkout only; obtain the explicit current-branch or task-branch choice and complete
approved document preparation under [handoff-prep](references/handoff-prep.md).
ARC-managed worktree execution is unsupported; report an isolated worktree request before dependent work.

contracts.heading: Implementer TDD and constraints
contracts.text:
## Implementer TDD and constraints

Before feature, bug-fix, or behavior edits, Implementer follows local `test-driven-development` unless the explicit
ARC exception applies; the Implementer profile holds Implementer's full TDD rules. TDD is waived only when every small,
low-risk criterion (Risk-scaled execution) and every plan-skip criterion (Orchestrator direct path) holds.
Before Implementer starts,
Orchestrator records the scope, why every criterion is met, acceptance criteria, and focused verification in the brief.
An explicit user or task-specific TDD request overrides
this waiver. For qualifying tasks only, this exception takes precedence over the generic trigger in the local reference;
do not change that skill. Ordinary multi-step or significant/high-risk work is not eligible. The waiver skips only
RED-GREEN steps; focused checks and risk-appropriate QA/Reviewer remain, and do not claim TDD was followed.
If a constraint blocks a required TDD step, Orchestrator records the
decision in the brief/plan and obtains any required human approval; internal approval is not a substitute.
Non-behavior documentation/configuration uses only a specifically authorized exception recorded in the brief; do not
generalize it to behavior work.

contracts.heading: Risk-scaled execution
contracts.text:
## Risk-scaled execution

Orchestrator assigns edits exclusively to Implementer except under the Orchestrator direct path below, and determines affected
behavior, risk,
and smallest meaningful verification.

| Risk | Minimum flow |
|---|---|
| Small, low risk | Implementer, or Orchestrator direct path → Orchestrator's focused checks → acceptance |
| Ordinary behavior | Implementer → independent QA → acceptance |
| Significant/high risk | Implementer → QA → independent Reviewer of the final full change → acceptance; with a plan, each plan task Implementer → FRESH QA → acceptance/commit satisfies the QA step, then independent Reviewer once on the final full change after all plan tasks |

Ordinary and significant plan tasks need a FRESH QA before acceptance; only small, low-risk tasks may be accepted on
Orchestrator focused checks. Small, low risk means narrow, understood, readily reversible, and verifiable by focused
checks. Ordinary behavior
fails those conditions without a significant-risk trigger. Significant risk includes shared role/behavior contracts,
shared state, lifecycle/integration order, security/permissions, data loss/migration, public interfaces, or costly
installation/deployment/rollback. Substantial behavior or contract changes are significant regardless of file count.
Unclear risk requires
investigation or the higher flow. Environment failure does not waive checks or determine design depth.

Do not add per-task gates automatically. Reviewer is never a plan-task acceptance prerequisite; for significant work
with a
plan, it reviews the final full change once after all plan tasks are accepted with their risk-scaled checks,
following the last plan task's required checks and any QA recheck at the final relevant state; significant work without
a plan
keeps Reviewer after QA before acceptance. Preserve specific approved obligations and complete risky dependency checks
before dependent implementation. Reuse evidence only when scope, relevant state, independence, freshness, and flow
position satisfy each covered requirement; changes, failures, or missing/conflicting evidence invalidate affected reuse.
QA checks independently without edits; Reviewer independently reads the final full change after QA for significant
work, without QA, planning, edits, delegation, or completion decisions. Orchestrator routes fixes to Implementer,
obtains affected QA rechecks outside the final plan Reviewer correction exception and required final review, and accepts after findings/evidence gaps are resolved or
explicitly dispositioned.

Criterion verdicts follow the Evidence verdict.

Authorization evidence and probe/combined scope are owned by [planning](references/planning.md#authorization-and-scope);
valid reuse and actual-state refresh by [handoff](references/handoff.md#authorization-continuity).
After gates hold, continue approved scope without saved documents through required checks and Orchestrator acceptance under
Completion continuity above; a role report alone does not complete the work.

contracts.heading: Orchestrator direct path for small tasks
contracts.text:
## Orchestrator direct path for small tasks

Orchestrator may edit directly only when every small, low-risk criterion (Risk-scaled execution) holds.
Every plan-skip criterion must also hold: one local change, no dependent stages, no cross-component shared state,
lifecycle, or integration-order concerns, and one focused verification path. Significant, architectural,
ordinary-behavior, unclear-risk work and edits overlapping a running Implementer's assigned files are ineligible.

Significant risk is defined in Risk-scaled execution and excludes work from the Orchestrator direct path;
do not infer eligibility from a small file count.

Before editing, Orchestrator records a scope record (not a brainstorming design) with scope and files,
why every criterion holds, acceptance criteria, and focused verification. Apply authorization in
[planning](references/planning.md#authorization-and-scope): an existing sufficiently specific user request can approve
that scope; no duplicate approval is needed. Otherwise present the scope record to the user and obtain explicit
approval before editing. Silence, an ambiguous response, or approval of other work is not approval.
Orchestrator then verifies the same handoff gate as a Implementer first start: explicit execution-target choice or valid
reuse, accessible intended workspace and repository, branch or detached HEAD, HEAD, staged/unstaged/untracked state,
preservation and ownership, and no unresolved failure or partial completion. Read the [handoff](references/handoff.md)
and [handoff preparation](references/handoff-prep.md) references before checking this gate.

Orchestrator edits only the approved files, preserves others' edits, and makes surgical changes without unrelated
refactoring or unapproved dependencies. Behavior edits follow the Implementer TDD rules and applicable recorded waiver
criteria; an explicit user or task-specific TDD request still requires test-driven-development.
Do not claim TDD under a waiver. After editing, Orchestrator records changed files, runs focused checks,
connects each acceptance criterion to evidence, and reports unverified scope. Orchestrator is not an independent
reviewer of its own edits; assign QA when evidence is incomplete. If scope expands, risk becomes unclear,
or any criterion fails, stop editing, record completed changes, and return subsequent edits to the normal Planner/Implementer
flow. A failed focused check or a QA finding routes the correction to Implementer, and it is rechecked; Orchestrator does not
self-correct.

Like other plan-skip
paths, there is no automatic task commit; commits follow applicable guidance and user requests.

contracts.heading: Token discipline and handoffs
contracts.text:
## Token discipline and handoffs

- Only Orchestrator invokes Claude native subagents or assigns specialist tasks. Give each invocation a descriptive role
  and bounded objective; the installed native profile determines its role and local model declarations.

- Keep one shared brief with fixed field order: Goal; Criteria (IDs); Exact scope/ownership (absolute workspace,
  branch or detached HEAD and HEAD, handoff record path, when one exists, files);
  Constraints/decisions; Evidence (paths/lines, commands, artifact links); Prior findings; Exact next objective (one
  bounded objective); Return format (conclusion, evidence locations, unresolved points, next step).
  On follow-ups send only changed fields and mark the rest `unchanged` (relative to a brief the recipient received);
  restart briefs follow handoff; a fresh specialist gets every other field in full. Send only the
  self-contained subset needed by the next role and links to accessible artifacts; omit full history, repeated
  instructions, and raw logs. No findings may be brief; requested deliverables such as complete plan drafts remain
  complete. Cite paths/lines/pages/commands/links instead of logs; investigate gaps only.
- `AskUserQuestion` questions use only `question`, a `header` of at most 12 characters, 2-4 `options` each with `label`
  and `description`, and `multiSelect`.
- Always start an ARC role by its installed native name (`arc-*`) with only the supplied scoped brief;
  never use a context-inheriting fork (such as the `fork` subagent type) for an ARC role; do not claim fresh context
  isolation without evidence. Reuse an existing specialist for related follow-up with only changed facts/objective when
  its context
  remains relevant; start fresh for unrelated or bloated context. Implementer and QA freshness follow the Role gate.
- Cite in the brief the absolute path of each required local ARC reference's SKILL.md (`test-driven-development` for Implementer,
  `brainstorming`/`writing-plans` for Planner); the role Reads it before dependent work.
- For Reviewer, Orchestrator writes the final base..HEAD diff plus changed-file list to
  `<git-common-dir>/arc/review/<slug>.diff` (same slug as the handoff record; base is the approved base HEAD recorded at
  handoff; inline when small or write denied) and cites its absolute path in the brief; Reviewer reads it and states
  limits. See verification.
- In Implementer briefs, cite the plan/spec path with the task section's line range and include only the needed excerpts,
  acceptance criteria, and constraints; do not ask Implementer to read whole plans or specs.
- Follow [Planner drafting preparation and consolidated feedback](planning.md#planner-drafting-preparation-and-consolidated-feedback).
  Complete the initial brief and whole-draft checklist before sending consolidated corrections. Gate further calls
  on documented changes or criterion progress; hold repetition without progress.
- Before optional calls, name the unresolved question and expected artifact. Skip calls whose questions are resolved
  by available evidence or direct inspection.
- Run each ARC role as a foreground Agent call and use its returned result, or run it in the background and wait for the
  completion notification; report unavailable execution to Orchestrator rather than inventing an API.
  Do not poll status in loops; never sleep-poll. A timeout or delay is not a reason to poll or check status in between.
  Send one complete brief per objective and batch related corrections. For long Bash commands set a sufficient `timeout`
  or use `run_in_background` and wait for its completion notification.

- Read only the needed ranges of files and outputs (for example `rg -n`, `sed -n`, `head`/`tail`) and cap long command
  output. Do not re-read files or outputs already in context unless they changed. A mandatory reference already read in
  this context and unchanged need not be re-read, and this skill file, once read in this context and unchanged,
  is not re-read on follow-up turns;
  this does not shorten any triggered mandatory reference read.
- When a plan completes or before starting another plan in a session with long history, Orchestrator records the
  canonical
  handoff state in the handoff record file and recommends that the user continue in a new session.
- Before handoff, post one short update with role/objective/expected output; after return, combine findings and next
  stage concisely. Do not expose hidden reasoning or raw prompts.

### Local superpowers references

Orchestrator briefs absolute paths under the selected installed ARC directory: Planner reads
`references/superpowers/brainstorming/SKILL.md` and `references/superpowers/writing-plans/SKILL.md`;
Implementer reads `references/superpowers/test-driven-development/SKILL.md`, including required relative references.
Resolve paths within each skill directory. Runtime needs no global discovery, external Skill invocation, or automatic download.
Missing/damaged local files stop dependent work: report exact paths to Orchestrator, without global fallback.
ARC approval, ownership, TDD exceptions and executor adapters still apply.
contracts.requiredBefore: Before the first specialist creation or assignment and related coordination decisions

contracts.heading: Models
contracts.text:
## Models

`models.toml` beside this skill is the source of truth for role model and reasoning-effort settings.
Configuration keys `arc_scouter`, `arc_planner`, `arc_implementer`, `arc_qa`, and `arc_reviewer` map to the hyphenated
Claude native subagent names above; they are not tool-call names.
Orchestrator uses the current conversation model. Use configured role settings without substitution or effort
reduction; report unavailable settings.
Local declarations do not prove runtime provider support, account access, alias resolution, actual model or effort
application, concurrency or depth enforcement.
New sessions reload profiles; running agents retain their current settings and parent relationships. Configuration
changes do not automatically reparent running agents or prove runtime parent behavior.

For browser visualization needs read [visual-companion](references/visual-companion.md). Use only capabilities
available within each role's exact allowlist; report unavailable capabilities and preserve unverified visual scope.
contracts.requiredBefore: Before the first specialist creation or assignment and related coordination decisions

contracts.heading: Dependency and readiness record
contracts.text:
After plan approval and before the first Implementer assignment, Orchestrator records all top-level task IDs in the
accessible canonical handoff record, linked to the approved plan version. For each task record explicit and implicit
predecessors, required inputs, outputs and shared contracts, owned files, conflicting shared resources, required
checks/QA path, ready/held status and reasons. Record the initial ready batch and capacity/serialization reasons.
Analyze shared APIs, contracts, generated artifacts and resources even when tasks edit different files. Unresolved
shared contracts or insufficient dependency information block the affected tasks; same-file concurrent Implementer edits
are blocked even for different lines. Do not infer independence from file separation or plan listing order.

A task is ready only when all applicable approvals and execution preparation are complete, required inputs/contracts
are available and settled, predecessors have required evidence and Orchestrator acceptance plus verified focused
commits (or accepted no-change records), ownership/resources do not conflict, its required check/QA path is available,
and a subagent slot exists under both the configured ARC full-tree cap shared by all roles and any lower actual runtime
limit (see [limits](limits.md)). Report runtime limits; ARC's cap is not a claim of runtime capability. Start all ready
independent tasks with fresh Implementers concurrently within capacity; record each hold or serialization reason instead of
silently following list order. Preserve existing risk gates, risk-scaled QA/Reviewer timing and execution-target
restrictions.

Update the map on completion, check evidence, acceptance, commit, slot return and new conflicts. Completion reports
alone do not release dependents. Reevaluate newly ready tasks immediately without waiting for unrelated batch members;
failed or ambiguous predecessors hold their dependent chain, while unaffected ready tasks may proceed. Dispatch still
passes [handoff](handoff.md) for each task, refreshing assignment evidence there; commits, shared-checkout Git
coordination and shared Git mutations follow [commit](commit.md). This record does not authorize
Orchestrator to rewrite Planner's approved task boundaries or waive approvals.

For example, with A → B → C and independent D and two slots, start A and D. After A's required checks,
Orchestrator acceptance and verified commit, start B while D continues if capacity and gates allow.
If A fails, hold B and C; D may continue if unaffected.

contracts.heading: Formal drafting boundary
contracts.text:
Orchestrator classifies scope before implementation. The Orchestrator direct path for small tasks is defined only in
[handoff](handoff.md#orchestrator-direct-path-for-small-tasks); follow it there and stop and reclassify if scope or risk changes.
Everything else follows this reference. Brainstorming and writing-plans are instructions for existing roles,
not extra agents; ARC routing and approval gates apply even if a skill names another executor.
Report a missing required skill before its stage; it blocks that stage. Integrate means save, route, and obtain approval; never author.
Significant risk is defined in [verification](verification.md#risk-scaled-execution).

contracts.heading: Design path and plan depth
contracts.text:
Record design and plan depth separately from verification risk. Risk determines checks and review, not the design path;
a bounded path or document omission does not imply low risk, and architectural depth adds no QA/Reviewer at every stage.

1. Before feature, design, or behavior changes, Orchestrator assigns Planner the local `brainstorming` skill with
   the brief and evidence. Planner returns the path (Spike, Bounded, or Architectural), design/options, trade-offs,
   acceptance criteria, assumptions, and focused questions. Orchestrator integrates, announces scope, routes
   answers/revisions, and obtains approvals; Orchestrator never runs brainstorming or writing-plans itself (SKILL.md
   Role gate); the direct path uses only a scope record.
2. Spike: apply Probe scope above; distinguish probe-only authorization from a sufficiently specified combined scope.
   Bounded: approve a short design before Implementer or an Orchestrator direct edit (Planner's design before
   Implementer; a direct edit uses only an approved scope record). Architectural: approve the design, then Planner returns a
   complete spec draft and self-review; Orchestrator integrates, saves (user's path or
   `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`), self-reviews, and obtains written-spec approval before
   implementation planning. Planner is read-only and cannot request approval.
3. After approved design/spec and before Implementer, Orchestrator assesses plan depth separately from file count, LOC,
   or bounded scope. Architectural work always uses `writing-plans` and a written plan approval, regardless of locality,
   risk, or size. For Bounded work skip the plan only for one local change with no dependent stages, cross-component
   shared state, lifecycle or integration-order concerns, and one focused verification path; otherwise require a draft.
   A "bounded" or "no plan" label does not bypass this judgment. "Orchestrator's recorded plan-depth judgment" means
   this assessment, including any Bounded written spec requirement, recorded in the brief.
4. Record dependencies and any plan-depth rationale in the brief. Planner returns the complete proportional plan,
   assumptions/open decisions, verification requirements, and self-review. Orchestrator integrates, saves to the user's
   path or `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`, self-reviews, and obtains plan approval before Implementer.
   Planner cannot save, implement, or request approval.
5. Every Implementer first start and restart requires all applicable approvals and the Common handoff gate (SKILL.md,
   handoff). Non-behavior configuration/documentation may skip inapplicable design/planning stages but not the gate.

When Orchestrator's recorded plan-depth judgment requires a Bounded written spec, record that and its scope,
use the approved short design as its basis, and have Planner return a proportional complete draft and self-review;
Orchestrator integrates, saves, self-reviews, and obtains individual written-spec approval before dependent plan
drafting. This applies that judgment, not a new spec rule. A required plan alone does not require a spec.

Design, spec, plan, and brainstorming drafts are authored only by Planner.
Orchestrator must not substitute its own spec for Planner's complete draft; return substantive omissions to Planner;
if Planner fails or is unavailable, stop and report, never draft instead. Design approval does not transfer ownership.

contracts.heading: Document-save evidence gates
contracts.text:
Before the first Architectural spec save, first required Bounded spec save, or first plan save, read this reference and
record accessible evidence in the brief or handoff record. Saving creates a reviewable file and does not require
written-spec approval; it requires valid execution-target choice and actual preparation; it is not approval or a commit, and an uncommitted file is never
described as committed.

**Spec save:** verify the approved design scope and approval evidence, Planner's complete spec draft and self-review,
Orchestrator's integration/save/review responsibility, and the absolute save path.
For a Bounded spec also verify the depth judgment, approved short design, and necessity rationale.
Saving or approving the short design does not replace the spec's drafting, self-review, or individual approval.

**Plan save:** verify the approved design and, when required, the approved spec version, Orchestrator's plan-depth
judgment, plan list and dependencies, Planner's complete draft and self-review, Orchestrator's responsibility,
and the absolute save path.

Missing or mismatched evidence stops the affected save; report to Orchestrator.

contracts.heading: Complete planning-document set
contracts.text:
The applicable set means all specs and plans required for the current approved execution scope.
Record scope, depth, absolute paths and coverage, approved versions, dependencies and order, skipped stages with
rationale, and documents awaiting writing or approval. The set is complete only when every required document is written
and individually approved and no unresolved decision needs another document.

A required plan does not itself require a written spec. Bounded uses Orchestrator's recorded plan-depth judgment;
spec steps apply only to Architectural and required Bounded specs. Preserve existing document omission rationales.

Claude v1 uses the current checkout or an approved task branch there; managed worktrees remain unsupported.

Normal order: initial design approval → execution-target choice → target preparation and verification →
formal spec drafting (when required), saving and self-review → written-spec approval → formal plan drafting
(when required), saving and self-review → individual plan approvals → complete applicable set → existing-commit
verification and one batch docs commit of remaining approved documents → final Git verification → Implementer handoff.
Written-spec approval precedes dependent plan drafting. On document-omission paths skip only the inapplicable document
steps; preserve target choice, preparation, state/ownership checks and Implementer gates.

contracts.heading: Focused commits (plan-task acceptance)
contracts.text:
Orchestrator reviews task evidence and accepts the approved task before committing.
Verify approved plan/task, absolute workspace, branch/HEAD, index/worktree/untracked state and ownership.
Stage exactly the accepted task paths; inspect staged scope and content to exclude unrelated changes.
After acceptance, Orchestrator creates the focused local commit without additional user commit approval.
After Orchestrator accepts a task, the next action is the required Git state/scope checks, staging, and focused commit.
Do not commit before task acceptance or defer the task commit until the plan ends.
Only Orchestrator accepts the task and executes its focused commit; Implementer completion does not replace acceptance.
Existing plan-skip paths have no new automatic commit obligation; their commits follow applicable guidance and user requests.

contracts.heading: Failure and external-action boundaries
contracts.text: On failure, stop dependent work and report actual state and completed steps. MUST NOT blindly repeat a commit or staging command. Push, merge, publish, deploy, and install still follow their separate guidance and approval rules. Implementer must not commit, even when explicitly assigned.
